method: Convex envelopes of planar cross-sections through registered HRA source surfaces constrain an optional loft. The cervical channel is anchored to the supplied external and internal cervical-os centers; the vaginal channel meets the same external-os landmark. Uterine inclination is retained. Tissue colors, relative thickness, luminal width and rugae are educational constructions, not source segmentations or measurements.

landmarks.coordinateSystem: meters, Y superior, X patient left, Z anterior; existing female registration

limits: Potential lumina are deliberately opened for visibility; depicted wall thickness, colors and fold amplitude are not measurements.
The convex envelope is a smooth teaching approximation and does not reproduce every concavity of the source exterior. Original geometry is retained separately and can be overlaid.
The upper vaginal/ectocervical mucosal connection is simplified; individual fornices and the epithelial transformation zone are not reconstructed.
The distal vaginal ring is an illustrative wall cut, not a reconstruction of the vaginal introitus or hymen. Vulva, labia and external genital microanatomy are outside this cutaway.
Uterine layers illustrate the corpus. Cervical mucosa and connective-tissue stroma are separately classified; the corpus endometrium is not continued down the vagina.
Endometrial cycle-dependent layers, glands, vessels, fine innervation and histological cells are not reconstructed. No menstrual phase is asserted.
Tubal and ovarian lumina/microanatomy are not added. Existing source tubes and ovaries remain context structures, with no artificial ovary-to-tube attachment.
Other organs retain their existing source substructures and surface clipping. No CT, MRI, patient-specific reconstruction or clinical validation.
originalGeometryScope: Diagram mode never modifies source geometry. Revision 13 independently repairs lung registration; genital diagram profiles and source anatomy remain unchanged.
